thesis: ASML's currently planned leading-edge lithography supply being below indicated 2027-2028 customer demand, combined with productivity-upgrade demand in its installed base, creates a two-channel fundamental mechanism: scarce new-system capacity can support pricing/mix and backlog conversion visibility while installed-base upgrades monetize customer wafer-capacity needs. If capacity can be expanded without disproportionate ramp costs or cancellations, medium-term earnings durability may be stronger than a generic semiconductor-equipment cycle would imply.
causal_chain: Leading-edge logic/DRAM customers increase medium-term capacity plans.
ASML's planned 2027-2028 supply is below stated customer demand.
Scarcity plus negotiated pricing/mix supports system economics, subject to conversion and cost discipline.
Installed-base productivity upgrades provide a second monetization channel for wafer-capacity demand.
Combined channels may improve medium-term revenue and margin durability.

test_contract.purpose: Independent documentary validation only; no economic outcome test is authorized.
required_checks: Re-run Legacy duplication screen against the pinned ledger and any newer durable negative-knowledge map.
Verify the 2027-2028 supply-demand statement and capacity-expansion baseline from primary ASML materials.
Distinguish customer interest, bookings/backlog and cancellable/non-cancellable commitments.
Assess whether pricing/mix and installed-base upgrades are structurally linked to the supply constraint rather than quarterly timing.
Stress export-control, customer-concentration, supplier-capacity, ramp-cost and AI-capex-reversal confounders.
Restrict or reject the claim if it reduces to generic AI-capex continuation or lacks incremental causal content.
falsification: Material order cancellations/push-outs or capex reductions break backlog conversion visibility.
Capacity ramp materially dilutes normalized gross margin or cannot be executed through suppliers.
Export controls block economically meaningful backlog conversion.
The thesis is duplicative of Legacy or cannot be distinguished from generic AI-demand exposure.
